evidence: Scope read in full: task/instruction.md (116 words, 3 paragraphs) and the six notes under task/environment/instructions (overview, policy, security, integration, behaviour, ui), plus seed_data.json. Spelling: I read every sentence and also extracted the complete unique-word list of the brief and notes (about 700 words) and inspected it; no misspelling found. Product names are spelled correctly (CodeMirror, Monaco, Ace, ProseMirror, TipTap, Quill, Slate, Draft.js, WebAssembly, SQLite). Spelling is consistently British across files (policy.md:5 'behaviour', ui.md:3 'behaviour', ui.md:13 'Colour'/'coloured'/'Colouring'; no 'color', 'behavior' or 'center' anywhere), so there is no mixed-dialect slip. Contamination: grep for TODO|FIXME|XXX|CHANGE_ME|placeholder|lorem|tbd, Windows or home-directory paths (C:\, F:/, /home/, /Users/), localhost/http URLs, and author/QC vocabulary (judge, rubric, criteri, golden, oracle, reviewer, QC, round ids) over the brief, notes and seed returned zero hits. The template stub 'CHANGE_ME: write the task prompt the agent receives.' is not present in the task brief. All files are pure ASCII, LF only, no BOM, no trailing or doubled spaces, no doubled words, and no sentence is duplicated within or across files (scripted check). The only paths mentioned are container paths that exist in the agent image: /instructions, /assets/seed_data.json, /app, /app/server.js, /app/app.db, /app/node_modules (Dockerfile: 'COPY instructions/ /instructions/', 'COPY assets/ /assets/', 'mkdir -p /app'). Internal consistency: instruction.md says 'Please read the six notes in /instructions' and exactly six .md files are shipped; cross-references 'as described in ui.md' (policy.md:3) and 'the boundary in security.md' (integration.md:5) point at files that exist. Single values throughout: one port (0.0.0.0:3000), one entry (node /app/server.js), one DB default (/app/app.db with DB_PATH override), one seed path, one health path, one run budget ('five-second run budget'), no accounts in any file ('without signing in' in instruction.md, 'without accounts' in overview.md, 'without sign-in or private accounts' in policy.md). The seed statement agrees in three places: instruction.md 'describes the starting scope; there is no starter app to finish', integration.md:7 'describes the starting scope and contains no user snippets or starter implementation', and seed_data.json '"snippets": []'. Library allowances agree: policy.md 'A parser or formatter library is fine', ui.md:3 'Parsing, highlighting and formatting libraries are allowed', ui.md:15 'A standalone formatter is allowed'. Network statements agree: integration.md:5 allows the app CDN assets 'but user-entered preview code has the boundary in security.md', and security.md 'The app itself may load public dependencies and assets'. Candidate contradictions I tested and rejected: (1) integration.md:3 'We start it with node /app/server.js' versus integration.md:9 'including when the app runs from a writable copy outside /app' - the note itself discloses the copy case and says 'Resolve files from their actual location', which matches tests/test.sh lines 92-100 (APP_ENTRY switches to the copy only when /app is not writable), so it is disclosed rather than contradictory. (2) behaviour.md:3 'Nothing from an earlier run ... carries into the next one' versus behaviour.md:5 restoring the last-good picture 'including values typed into its controls' - the first governs a new run, the second what is displayed after a failed run, and 'A restored picture may be static' removes the conflict. (3) ui.md:9 'A run of ordinary single-caret typing may be undone in one step or character by character' versus the multi-caret burst being one Undo action - different cases, explicitly distinguished. (4) policy.md 'You may choose the layout, labels' versus ui.md:17 listing the controls to include - a list of functions, not fixed label text. Minor observation, not a defect: policy.md:5 says 'The examples are ways to explain it, not exact selectors, CSS classes or implementation requirements' although the notes contain no selectors or classes; it reads as a disclaimer, not as pasted-in material. This row is static and does not depend on runtime evidence; no run was needed or used for the verdict.
